citations.B1: Check-then-set race: two threads can both read `count < limit` and both write, exceeding the limit
citations.B3: hold a lock around read+write (or use an atomic store increment)
citations.B4: No time window: counts never reset, so every user is permanently blocked after `limit` requests for the process lifetime
citations.B5: Unbounded memory: every distinct `user_id` stays in the dict forever
citations.B6: `counts` is per-process, so N workers each grant `limit`, giving N×limit in aggregate
citations.B7: `user_id` is not validated: unhashable values raise `TypeError` and `None` or empty IDs collapse into one shared bucket
